claim: Standard RLVR training with a binary correctness reward is indifferent to confidence, providing no penalty for confident-but-wrong predictions, thereby degrading calibration by construction.
stance_target: binary correctness reward structurally cannot produce calibration
quoted_support: Standard reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) trains models with a binary correctness reward that is indifferent to confidence, providing no penalty for confident but wrong predictions and thereby degrading calibration.

claim: Verbalized confidence is calibrated only at the token level and exhibits inconsistency across textual variations that share the same semantic meaning -- the central motivating gap CSR is built to close.
stance_target: verbalized confidence tokens robustly reflect underlying model uncertainty regardless of surface phrasing
scope_conditions: verbalized-confidence RL methods evaluated across paraphrase variation
quoted_support: However, verbalized confidence is calibrated at the token level and thus exhibits inconsistency across textual variations with same semantic meaning.
